prompt.context: Your client is FlashPro Inc., a San Francisco based technology company that develops and sells wearable and mountable action cameras. FlashPro's CEO believes that the company's growth has stagnated and has hired your firm to remedy that issue.
prompt.question: FlashPro's growth has stagnated. How would you approach diagnosing and solving this problem?

clarifying_info.q: Is FlashPro a public or private company?
Where does FlashPro sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: It sells products in the US and internationally.
Their main product is CamPro, a mounted camera mainly used when playing action sports. It has also recently started being used in other recreational activities.

clarifying_info.q: Does FlashPro manufacture its own products?
clarifying_info.a: FlashPro does not manufacture its products; it contracts with manufacturers in China.

clarifying_info.q: What sales channels does FlashPro use?
clarifying_info.a: FlashPro sells through three channels: Distributors, Retail, and FlashPro's Website.
The industry is highly competitive and customers are very loyal to each brand.
COGS have remained steady at 50% of total sales.

exhibits.title: Action Camera Potential Market in the US
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the total addressable action camera market size in the US (in thousands of customers) from 2013 actual through 2019 estimated.

exhibits.title: Action Camera Market Penetration in the U.S.
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the percentage of the US addressable market that has purchased an action camera, from 2013 actual through 2019 estimated.

exhibits.title: 2016 Action Camera Market Share Distribution
exhibits.shows: A pie chart showing each competitor's share of the action camera market. Note states market share distribution is the same in the US and worldwide and has been steady for 5 years, and FlashPro is the only company offering wearables.

exhibits.title: New Market Entry Comparison
exhibits.shows: A table comparing four potential new country markets across current market size, FlashPro's expected year-1 market share, expected annual growth over the next 3 years, and sales channel distribution (Distributors / Retail / FlashPro Website).

data.note: After year 3, expected market annual growth for all countries is 5%. Dollar amounts in thousands.

framework: Market Analysis: Competitors, Customers, Substitutes, Suppliers — assess competitive dynamics and loyalty
Profitability Tree: Break down Revenue (price x volume, by channel/geography) and Costs (COGS, R&D, G&A, Sales & Marketing)
Revenue Growth Levers: Product Mix (4 Ps — advertising, product attributes, channels, price), New Markets (geographies, product line expansion), Organic vs. Inorganic (M&A)
New Market Assessment: Size, growth, competitive landscape, channel economics, entry barriers

questions.prompt: Question 1: What is FlashPro's expected Gross Profit for 2017? (Hand out Exhibits 1–3)
questions.guidance: Candidate should build up US revenue from addressable market x penetration x market share x price, then derive international revenue using the 60/40 US/international split. Apply 50% COGS to total revenue to get gross profit.

math.setup: US Camera Sales = Addressable Market × Penetration × FlashPro Market Share × Price; International = US Sales × (40/60); Total Revenue = US + International; COGS = 50% × Total Revenue; Gross Profit = Total Revenue − COGS. All amounts in thousands.

questions.prompt: Question 2: What are FlashPro's revenue growth prospects, and what other alternatives could help boost the top line?
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe from Exhibits 1–3 that US market growth is slowing (curve flattening) and competition is fierce (30% share with loyal customers), limiting organic market-share gains. Then brainstorm structured growth levers: (1) Product Mix / 4 Ps — advertising, product attributes, channels, pricing; (2) New Markets — new geographies or product line expansion; (3) Organic development vs. Inorganic (M&A). If candidate does not raise new geographies, guide them toward it and hand out Exhibit 4.

questions.prompt: Question 3: From an economic perspective, which country is most attractive to enter, and what should FlashPro consider before entering? (Hand out Exhibit 4)
questions.guidance: Calculate Year-3 revenue for each country by growing the current market at the stated rate for 3 years, then applying FlashPro's Year-1 market share. An excellent candidate notes that a higher share of sales through FlashPro's own website implies higher margins (no intermediary), making the channel mix a secondary criterion. Best answer: Argentina ($1,165K year-3 revenue, 50% website channel).

math.setup: Year-N market = Current Size × (1 + growth)^N; FlashPro Year-3 revenue = Year-3 market × Year-1 market share (share assumed constant). All amounts in thousands.
math.answer: Argentina yields the highest Year-3 revenue at ~$1,165K and has 50% of sales through FlashPro's Website (highest margin channel). Argentina is the most attractive entry market.

brainstorming.prompt: What are different ways FlashPro can grow its revenues and profits?

categories.name: Product Mix (4 Ps)
ideas: Improve product attributes (battery life, video quality, durability, wearable form factor)
Expand or optimize sales channels (e.g., grow direct/website to improve margins)
Adjust pricing strategy (premium positioning, bundles, accessories)

categories.name: New Markets — New Geographies
ideas: Enter high-growth international markets (e.g., Argentina, Sweden)
Target regions where action sports are growing rapidly
Leverage existing manufacturing relationships to reduce incremental costs

categories.name: New Markets — Product Line Expansion
ideas: Develop accessories (mounts, cases, batteries, editing software)
Launch a consumer-grade lower-price camera to capture a broader segment
Expand into adjacent categories (drones, body cameras, automotive cameras)
Offer software/subscription services (cloud storage, video editing)

categories.name: Organic Growth
ideas: Invest in R&D to maintain wearable differentiation (currently the only wearable player)
Build out FlashPro's direct website channel to improve margins
Deepen customer loyalty programs to reduce churn

categories.name: Inorganic Growth (M&A)
ideas: Acquire a competitor to consolidate market share
Acquire a technology company to accelerate product development
Acquire a distribution company to improve channel economics

recommendation: FlashPro should enter Argentina: it offers the highest projected Year-3 revenue (~$1,165K) and a sales channel mix heavily weighted toward FlashPro's own website (50%), implying higher margins than the other candidate markets.
In parallel, FlashPro should leverage its unique wearable positioning to defend and grow US market share through product differentiation and direct-channel expansion.
risks: Entry cost analysis was not included — market entry requires investment in marketing, logistics, and local operations that could erode the revenue advantage
Year-1 market share assumptions (35% for Argentina) may be aggressive given brand loyalty dynamics in a new market
Currency and geopolitical risk in Argentina (economic volatility, FX controls)
Competitive response from incumbent local players
next_steps: Conduct deeper due diligence on the Argentinian market: customer habits, local competition, regulation, economic and geopolitical situation, and logistics
Develop a full P&L model for Argentina entry including marketing, distribution, and operational costs
Design a go-to-market plan for Argentina covering advertising, sales channel setup, promotional strategy, and supply chain logistics
